required_assertions.text: NyssaBench is an open-source failure-aware evaluation and audit framework for embodied AI policies, built toward foundational infrastructure for evaluating frontier robot systems.

forbidden_assertions: NyssaBench is foundational infrastructure for failure-aware evaluation

claims.wording: NyssaBench is an open-source failure-aware evaluation and audit framework for embodied AI policies, built toward foundational infrastructure for evaluating frontier robot systems.
limitations: This positioning describes the implemented framework, not frontier-policy performance or sim-real predictive validity.

claims.wording: NyssaBench executes typed stressors and records requested, applied, unsupported, and backend-confirmed condition evidence.
limitations: Support is stressor, engine, task, and observation-mode specific; a declared stressor is not evidence that a backend applied it.

claims.wording: NyssaBench records temporally ordered FailureEvents with evidence visibility, provenance, causal hypotheses, and recovery eligibility.
limitations: A FailureEvent causal-parent field is a hypothesis unless separate intervention evidence supports causality.

claims.wording: NyssaBench can compare matched continuation and recovery branches when the simulator, policy, stressors, and random streams expose defensible restoration contracts.
limitations: Strong causal language is unavailable for qualified or unsupported state restoration.

claims.wording: NyssaBench separates reproducible run validity from executable benchmark-validity audits.
limitations: A validator passing on synthetic fixtures does not establish that a reference benchmark has passed the audits.

claims.wording: NyssaBench evaluates external runtime failure monitors under versioned deployable or privileged contracts.
limitations: The built-in action-magnitude monitor is an integration control, not an interpretability method or learned baseline.

claims.wording: NyssaBench produces prespecified pass, fail, inconclusive, or invalid checkpoint regression decisions over pinned paired evidence.
limitations: A policy release decision is not a public benchmark rank or deployment-safety certification.

claims.wording: Nyssa Evaluation Protocol 0.1 defines six versioned, content-addressed evaluation contracts with executable cross-contract claim validation.
limitations: NEP 0.1 is not a published protocol release until the package/release workflow executes.
The committed ManiSkill fixture is schema conformance, not GPU execution evidence.

claims.wording: NyssaBench validates external policy metadata, lifecycle, observations, actions, horizons, deterministic resets, and smoke artifacts before full evaluation.
limitations: Conformance is task, engine, checkpoint, and contract specific and does not establish a validated reference track.

claims.wording: NyssaBench has validated reference tracks for materially different learned and frontier policy families.
artifact_requirements: paired clean and shifted result packs
promotion_requirements: Complete issue #16 with at least two learned policy families on the same held-out benchmark subset.
Pass leakage, action-contract, paired-seed, and replay evidence checks.
limitations: Current random, scripted, BC, RoboMimic, LeRobot, VLA, and diffusion entries include controls or adapter paths that are not validated frontier tracks.

claims.wording: NyssaBench provides a compact, diverse reference benchmark with protected split lineage and solvability evidence.
promotion_requirements: Complete issue #17 and pass shortcut, contamination, split-lineage, and solvability audits.
limitations: Existing suites and task counts do not satisfy the compact reference benchmark claim.

claims.wording: NyssaBench continuously validates MuJoCo and GPU-backed ManiSkill execution in CI.
promotion_requirements: Complete issue #19 with scheduled MuJoCo and capable-runner ManiSkill jobs.
Measure flakiness before making simulator jobs required gates.
limitations: Current pull-request CI proves Python behavior and mocked contracts, not full GPU simulator execution.

claims.wording: NyssaBench executes versioned paired sim-real studies over content-pinned simulation runs and validated real-evidence packages.
limitations: The analysis module does not supply hardware evidence or authorize a predictive sim-real claim.

claims.wording: NyssaBench failure profiles and counterfactual recoverability predict real robot behavior beyond clean simulation success.
promotion_requirements: Complete the hardware calibration track in #20.
Complete the paired SimRealStudy implementation in #38.
Report a well-powered positive or negative held-out result.
limitations: No current result pack supports a sim-real predictive claim.

claims.wording: NyssaBench is foundational infrastructure for failure-aware evaluation of frontier embodied AI policies.
promotion_requirements: Pass the machine-readable Phase 1 credibility gate in #30.
Complete every claim named by promotion_gate.required_claim_ids.
Promote this wording in a separate reviewed change after evidence is pinned.
limitations: This is milestone wording and is not authorized as the current project claim.

promotion_gate.milestone_wording: NyssaBench is foundational infrastructure for failure-aware evaluation of frontier embodied AI policies.
